title: Modern statutory settlement
documented_fact: The British Museum Act 1963 provides the modern statutory architecture, including separate Natural History trustees and statutory collection/repository provisions.
why_it_matters: This is constitutive evidence: it tells us what Parliament made the institution legally responsible for, rather than how later managers describe it.
limit_or_continuity: The present administrative framework remains downstream of the Act.

title: Current sponsor framework
documented_fact: The DCMS framework sets out the contemporary sponsor, finance, appointment and accountability relationship.
why_it_matters: It is evidence of current administrative machinery, not the source of the Museum's underlying statutory powers.
limit_or_continuity: The framework itself says it does not create legal powers/responsibilities.
